ora·ïto — projects — Beaugrenelle Cinema

Beaugrenelle Cinema

Category Architecture
Brand Pathé
Collection Pathé
Year 2013

Because a film is a journey, a constantly renewed experience, the Pathé cinemas designed by Ora-ïto invite you to the boarding area. Without a suitcase but with his mind turned towards the horizon, the viewer is welcomed into a space designed like an airport of the future. Counters and ticketing terminals, waiting and relaxation areas, ticket checking and access to dark rooms... Everything contributes to pleasure, relaxation and excitement. Ready for flight?

The first of its kind is located on the banks of the Seine, in the renewal of the Beaugrenelle center. Through this “Parisian flagship”, Ora-ïto displays its vision of “another cinema” and revolutionizes current codes, but also the consumption patterns of film buffs.

The architecture is refined but optimized, traditional posters have become animated digital screens, the reception hall is open to the street thanks to its large bay windows and offers its visitors a multitude of services including a café with a view, a concierge and educational workshops for children. The course itself is innovative; no more queues, more sensory signage and an exhilarating universe transporting our imagination to another dimension!

For the first time in its history, Gaumont-Pathé, the number one French cinema, is entrusting its visual identity to a designer.

The choice fell on Ora-ïto. The sculptural Pathé Beaugrenelle is only the first step in a great step forward. Around ten multiplexes are currently in development throughout France, the openings of which will follow one another in the coming months. Marseille Plan de Campagne already has its own and will open it in a few weeks. This year, the French giant and the Ora-ïto brand are writing a story together, much more than a feature film or a series but a true cosmic saga revolutionizing today's cinema to offer that of tomorrow.

Because “the first of films is the river” (Jean Renoir), space unfolds with cinematic fluidity. The journey that leads the viewer from the reception hall to their seat is similar to a tracking shot. The soft dramatization of the spaces still offers panoramic views and low angles. In its own way, architecture here is a cinema course. Before the lights go out in the theaters, the show has already started. Upon entering the reception hall, the visitor is immediately absorbed into a scenario. The entire architecture aims to showcase the cinematic promise and its desire for escape. The undulating wave, structuring the ceiling, protects, envelops and caresses the spectators. The choice of materials warms you up, Corian® mixed with oak wood offers the perfect combination of an authentic and reassuring atmosphere. We are then immersed in a journey with fluid shapes, guided intuitively and become the actors of a sequence worthy of a “box office” production. The hall turns into a stage. All the elements, terminals, ticketing, seats and counters emerge from the ground, growing like plants. They are “naturally” in their place and contribute to a climate of relaxation and excitement.

Largely glazed on two sides, the hall offers views of the exterior. The pleasure of airports where everyone can follow the takeoff of planes is thus continually renewed. But in Beaugrenelle, it is the urban spectacle, in all its clarity, which becomes a prelude to diving into the projection rooms. Ora-ïto creates the lobby as a layering of spaces. The shots stand out from each other, follow one another, are superimposed as if editing a film work. From all sides, the gaze selects and embraces the volumes in their otherness: reception, bar, relaxation areas, walls of sweets... Thanks to their architectural treatment, the activity centers are clearly identifiable and delimited. The areas are circumscribed. The flows of spectators are gently framed by the division of the floor, reinforced by the different colors of the walls and the intensity of the lighting. The flow of spectators and the flow of the image combine. The bodily experience of the cinema complex is an introduction to the 7th art.

With its demarcated zones and its buffer spaces within which the spectator moves without thinking, with its junctions, its gentle breaks, the Pathé Beaugrenelle multiplex is a real city in reduction where its neighborhoods, its public spaces, its main square, its airs of rest and waiting, (the reception bench is the central sculpture of the lobby, profiled like a windsurfing board) mingle, its street corners and its basements. At the end of a dizzying escalator, the underside of which lights up, wide corridors, an enveloping and airy atmosphere are united in a deep but warm black. A monumental wall sculpture playing with light in a kinetic way brings together the different open walkways like the decks of a boat. The viewer is captured in an accelerated perspective which generates a whistle effect. Floor and ceiling seem to come together, as if captured by the eye of a director. The focal length closes, the show is about to begin. Reference to film noir, black and white, dark rooms? The imagination is unbridled. To each their own feature film.

Luxury is offered to all and finds its signature in the announced excitement of the champagne bar which adjoins the rooms in the basement. The yellow polka dot carpet, of various sizes, seems to be dotted with pixel-style confetti, thus offering dotted and playful points of light, and information screens in front of the rooms complete the system. Cutting-edge technology leads to dreams. Because, after the airport and its departure lounges, here come the hotel rooms. The access to the rooms, with their organic curves and their futuristic alcoves with backlit numbers, arouse the curiosity of its visitors and invite them to discover a masterful work. The experience is not only on the other side, but is also around these arches that generate emotion before each screening. Behind the heavy doors, redesigned and equipped with metallic handles with sensual curves, the cinemas are so many intimate worlds where everyone can relax in optimal comfort. The dream is a journey, so is the cinema. On the wings of desire, everyone can languish and settle down. In an individual seat or in a seat intended for couples, as for films, the choice is on the program.

In its range of colors layered and modulated according to four references: gray, yellow, white and wood, the reception hall offers its warm atmosphere without effusion. The right temperature, the right climate… sunny. The work of lights fully participates in this. A floral, daisy halo, all yellow drowned in whiteness, plunges us into a spring world, clear and pleasant. These references all come from the yellow rooster, the historic emblem of Pathé. Even more so when it is animated in the famous credits, with its Calder-style mobile, its play of projected shadows, the graphics are found symbolically throughout the complex imagined by Ora-ïto. From the door handles to the design of the seats arranged like levitating pebbles and the resumption, on the floor, of the ceiling elements, thus drawing oblong tablecloths designed in mirror (white on the ceiling, wood on the floor or vice versa...), Ora-ïto has seized the movement inscribed in the DNA of Pathé cinema. Its architecture swings like a mobile. The solid presence of the materials joins the evanescence of the cinematographic dream. The entire variation of decorative elements is thus stamped with the seal of legitimacy.

• 10 rooms with 141 to 376 seats for a total of 1,933 seats
• One of the largest screens in Paris: 18 meters base
• 7.1 digital sound in all rooms, and the only Parisian cinema with two rooms equipped with the Dolby Atmos sound system, the latest audio technology for total immersion within the film
• Two rooms equipped with 4K projection, for a resolution twice that of traditional digital projection and 4 rooms equipped with the Dolby 3D system
• An accentuated gradation of the rooms to enjoy the session in complete peace and quiet without being bothered by your neighbor in front
• A space of 1.10 meters between each row
• A choice of seats and numbered chairs
• Duos armchairs with lifting armrests to enjoy a session for two
• A Champagne bar
• An innovative offering of additional products and services
